text:
Alex: Hey team — first day. Trying to build the inference runtime from source inside the dev Docker image and hitting a linking error from nvcc. Followed the README (cuda:12.2 base image, gcc 11). Anyone can point me to the usual troubleshooting steps?

Alex: build snippet:
```bash
docker run --gpus all -v $(pwd):/src -w /src redwood/dev:cuda-12.2 make -j16
[ 12%] Linking CXX executable llm_serving
nvcc fatal   : Value 'sm_86' is not valid for option 'gpu-name'
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcuda
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

Alex: I tried make clean + rebuild, same error. I'm on a company laptop with driver installed via package manager.

Mika: welcome onboard! :tada: quick checks: run `nvidia-smi` on host and `nvcc --version` inside the container. usually this is a driver/toolkit mismatch.

Natanael: +1. If `-lcuda` is missing it's often the host driver < container toolkit. Driver needs to support the toolkit version. Check host driver version (nvidia-smi) >= required by CUDA 12.x (usually 525+).

Rosie: also check CUDA_ARCH_LIST / GPU arch flags. If your GPU is older/newer, nvcc may choke on sm_86. You can override with `export CUDAARCHS=sm_80,sm_86` or set `-DCUDA_ARCH_NAME=Manual` in CMake.

Alex: running `nvidia-smi` now: Driver Version: 520.61.05
Alex: inside container `nvcc --version` shows CUDA 12.2

Mika: yup that's it — driver 520 < toolkit expectation. Two options: downgrade container toolkit to 12.1 image that works with 520, or update host driver to 525+. If you don't want to update the laptop, use the `redwood/dev:cuda-12.1` image for now.

Alex: ok I'll try switching images. If I update the driver, any tips?

Natanael: update via the distro package or the driver installer. On Linux we prefer the package-managed driver from our internal driver repo so the kernel modules match. Ping infra if you need sudo.

Rosie: also if you hit ptxas/gpu-name errors you can temporarily add `-gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80` to CXX flags, but that's a band-aid.

Alex: switching to `redwood/dev:cuda-12.1` fixed the linker stage and the binary is building. Thanks!

Mika: awesome. When you have a sec, add your laptop/driver combo to the onboarding checklist (so we can add common combos). Here's the onboarding doc: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/runtime-build (internal).

infra-bot: Note: opened ticket INFRA-412 to track driver-image compatibility checks across dev images.

Alex: Will do — appreciate all the help. Tagging @Mika @Natanael if I run into follow-ups. :thumbsup:
